content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm trying to configure a button so that pressing it the first time sets an input high, and pressing it again turns the input off. I've added a button and experimented with options like "SetBit" and "InvertBit" under various events (such as Click, Press, Release, Activate, etc). Additionally, I included a visual indicator to display the input state by color change. I attempted different approaches, but the input only remains high for a brief moment when the button is pressed. Currently, I'm using [product_name][version_no] together with [product_name][version_no] and a [product_name] panel. Any suggestions on how I can resolve this issue? Thanks in advance!
Hello [user_name], Are you working with an Input tag? Try using a Flag instead. Direct Inputs can be overwritten by [product_name] every cycle. Best regards,

Hello [user_name], Thanks for your reply. Could you clarify what you mean by using a flag? Should it be implemented in the PLC program or in the HMI visualization? The PLC program is already complete (written by a former colleague) and I want to simulate both the original inputs and outputs via the HMI for testing purposes. Everything should be testable without the actual machine (see attached file). Appreciate your help!

Hello [user_name], The flag should be created in the PLC program so the HMI can write to it. If your aim is to simulate the [product_name] program, you can do so with [product_name]. This allows you to select inputs and monitor program responses. Best regards,

Hello [user_name], I've added the flag as shown in the attachment and set up the button event, but it still isn't working. I might be making a conceptual mistake (we use the term often in Holland, not sure about English). Regarding testing, I'm aware of the simulation option, but I prefer it working as described for actual machine testing. This program needs to communicate with a unit and I want to test PLC/HMI functionality with the unit directly, without relying on the machine or laptop—also helpful for future debugging and error tracking. Thank you!
Hello [user_name], If you're using "Input 1" and "M1", connect both to an OR function; the result should feed into your desired AND function. Best regards,
Thank you! That solves my issue, so I can continue with the project (and will likely encounter more questions along the way). Hope you have a great day!

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered difficulties toggling an input using an HMI button for simulation purposes, as the input remained active only briefly. Advice was given to use a flag within the PLC program—written by a previous colleague—to prevent overwriting of Input states, clarifying the distinction between visualization/HMI configuration and PLC logic. Additional help addressed logical connections required for reliable toggling, with final confirmation that the solution worked for the intended hardware simulation scenario.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the HMI button to consistently toggle an input high or low, effectively simulating the hardware for reliable debugging and testing, independent of the physical machine.
pain_keywords: unclear difference between flags and direct inputs
